mcqs.q: Fixed prosthodontics restores teeth with prostheses that are:
opts: Cemented or attached to the teeth and NOT removable by the patient
Removed and cleaned by the patient every night
Only used for children's primary teeth
Always made of acrylic and rest on the gums
mcqs.explain: Fixed prostheses are cemented (or implant-attached) and cannot be removed by the patient — unlike removable dentures.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a FIXED restoration?
mcqs.explain: A crown is a fixed (cemented) restoration; the others are removable appliances.

mcqs.q: A post & core is mainly used to:
opts: Rebuild a badly broken, root-canal-treated tooth so it can retain a crown
Replace an entire missing tooth in the arch
Cover only the biting surface of a molar
mcqs.explain: The post anchors in the root canal and the core rebuilds coronal structure to support a crown.

mcqs.q: A laminate veneer is best described as:
opts: A thin facing used mainly for anterior esthetics
A full-coverage metal restoration for molars
An artificial tooth suspended between two abutments
A titanium fixture placed into bone
mcqs.explain: Veneers are thin facings bonded to the front of (usually anterior) teeth for esthetics.

mcqs.q: A fixed dental prosthesis (bridge) is used to:
opts: Replace one or more missing teeth by cementing to prepared abutment teeth
Restore a single cavity within the cusps
mcqs.explain: A bridge replaces missing teeth and is cemented onto adjacent prepared abutments.

opts: A titanium fixture placed in bone to support a crown
mcqs.explain: An implant is an osseointegrated titanium fixture that supports a crown/prosthesis.

mcqs.q: Which crown material generally gives the BEST esthetics?
mcqs.explain: All-ceramic crowns are the most esthetic; PFM balances esthetics and strength; metal is strongest but least esthetic.

mcqs.q: A porcelain-fused-to-metal (PFM) crown is chosen because it offers:
opts: A combination of esthetics and strength
No need for any tooth preparation
mcqs.explain: PFM combines a metal substructure (strength) with a porcelain veneer (esthetics).

mcqs.q: The main purpose of a provisional (temporary) crown is to:
opts: Protect the prepared tooth and maintain esthetics/function until the final crown
mcqs.explain: Provisionals protect the prepared tooth and preserve esthetics, function and tooth position between prep and cementation.

mcqs.q: In a fixed bridge, the artificial tooth that replaces the missing tooth is the:
mcqs.explain: Pontic = the artificial replacement tooth; it sits over the edentulous ridge.

mcqs.q: The prepared natural tooth that SUPPORTS a bridge is the:
mcqs.explain: The abutment is the prepared supporting tooth; the retainer is cemented onto it.

mcqs.q: The part of a bridge that joins the pontic to the retainer is the:
mcqs.explain: Connectors join the pontic to the retainers on either side.

opts: Cover the external surface of the tooth (e.g. full or partial crowns)
Fit entirely within the tooth's anatomical contours
Are always removable by the patient
mcqs.explain: Extracoronal = covering the outside of the crown (full/partial veneer crowns).

mcqs.q: Intracoronal restorations are defined as those that:
opts: Fit within the anatomical contours of the clinical crown
Cover all external surfaces of the tooth
Are supported by a titanium implant
mcqs.explain: Intracoronal restorations (inlays/onlays) sit within the tooth's contours.

mcqs.q: The key difference between an onlay and an inlay is that an onlay:
opts: Covers one or more cusps, whereas an inlay does not
Is always made of gold, whereas an inlay is ceramic
Replaces a missing tooth, whereas an inlay does not
Is removable, whereas an inlay is fixed
mcqs.explain: An inlay lies between the cusps; an onlay additionally covers one or more cusps.

mcqs.q: The course carries a total of 6 credit hours, made up of:
mcqs.explain: Credit hours = 6 (2 lecture + 4 laboratory); contact hours 28 lecture + 112 lab = 140.

mcqs.q: To pass the course, a student must:
opts: Score ≥ 60% overall AND pass theory and practical separately
Score ≥ 60% overall only, regardless of components
mcqs.explain: ≥60% aggregate, plus ≥40% of the theory final and ≥50% aggregate of the practical — passed separately.

mcqs.q: Identify the labelled parts of this implant restoration (top → bottom):
mcqs.explain: From the visible crown down: crown (top) → abutment (middle) → implant fixture in bone (bottom).

saqs.q: Define fixed prosthodontics and list the five main types of fixed restoration.
saqs.a: Fixed prosthodontics is the art and science of restoring damaged teeth and replacing missing teeth with prostheses that are cemented/attached and not removable by the patient. Five types: crown, post & core, laminate veneer, fixed dental prosthesis (bridge), and dental implant.

saqs.q: Name the four parts of a fixed bridge and define each.
saqs.a: Abutment = the prepared supporting tooth; Retainer = the crown/restoration cemented onto the abutment; Pontic = the artificial tooth replacing the missing one (over the edentulous ridge); Connector = joins the pontic to the retainer.

saqs.q: Differentiate extracoronal from intracoronal restorations, giving an example of each.
saqs.a: Extracoronal restorations cover the external surface of the tooth (e.g. full-veneer/complete crown, partial-veneer crown). Intracoronal restorations fit within the anatomical contours of the clinical crown (e.g. inlay, onlay).

saqs.q: Differentiate an inlay from an onlay.
saqs.a: An inlay restores a cavity lying between the cusps and does not cover a cusp. An onlay is similar but additionally covers one or more cusps.

saqs.q: List three crown materials with one property of each, and state the purpose of a provisional crown.
saqs.a: All-ceramic — best esthetics; PFM — esthetics plus strength; metal (gold) — maximum strength with least tooth reduction (also all-resin, stainless-steel). A provisional crown protects the prepared tooth and maintains esthetics, function and tooth position until the final crown is cemented.
